target_sector: Our target market includes high-end artisanal cheese aficionados, wine bars, restaurants, cheese enthusiasts, wine drinkers, and everyday consumers. In Japan, the consumption of premium artisanal cheeses has steadily grown as Western food culture influences increase through globalization and tourism. High-quality cheeses are featured in top European restaurants, and more Japanese consumers are pairing them with fine wines. Cheese consumption in Japan grew after 1964 and the Tokyo Olympics, with the popularity of Italian dishes like pizza and pasta. Despite the steady growth of domestic cheese demand, Japan relies heavily on imports, covering only 12.1% of cheese production in 2020. To reduce dependence on imports, the Japanese Ministry of Agriculture has incentivized local farmers to sell raw milk to cheese producers. However, with increasing demand for high-end cheeses, Japan's cheese market remains dependent on imported artisanal products.
specialities: We sell our cheeses in our high-end food products shops “Fromagerie MACU The Shop”, and also cook delicious recipes with it in our restaurant “Fromagerie MACU” based in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. We also sell it to other high-end restaurants in Ulaanbaatar and in Hong Kong.

exhibited_products: We produce and sell Mongolian artisanal cheeses. For Foodex, we will present our flagship product, Khustai Gouda, the oldest and premier Mongolian cheese, made continuously for 30 years in the Khustai National Park. Produced by Tumurkhuyag Urtnasan and his family since 1995, it comes from a remote, nomadic area 80 km southwest of Ulaanbaatar. Khustai Gouda is unique for several reasons. The milk used comes from cows grazing on wild forbs in high-altitude pastures. This summer milk is rich in proteins and minerals, giving the cheese its distinctive flavor. Handmade in small batches, the cheese is salted and aged for 2-3 months in a wooden shed before further maturation near Ulaanbaatar. Some batches age up to 18 months, resulting in a firm, crumbly texture and a flavor that evolves from mild and slightly salty to rich, nutty, and caramelized with umami notes. Unlike industrial Gouda, it contains no preservatives or additives, reflecting the pure taste of Mongolian milk. Khustai Gouda stands out for its exceptional quality and pairs well with wine, enhancing dishes like fondue and pasta.
